property_summary: After any sequence of calls to Put, the sum of all msg.value sent across all Put invocations must equal the sum of Acc[addr].balance across all addresses minus initial balances.
After any call to Put, the balance of the caller in Acc must be at least as large as the amount of Ether sent in that call.

After a call to Put, the sum of all Acc balances plus total Ether sent in failed Collect calls must equal the contract's Ether balance; the mutant violates this invariant by not increasing the caller's Acc balance on Put, causing a mismatch between internal accounting and actual Ether held.

After any call to Put, the caller's Acc balance must be at least the total msg.value sent by that caller across all their Put calls; the mutant never increases the balance, so any caller who makes a second Put call will have a balance strictly less than their total sent Ether.
After a successful Put call, the caller's balance must equal the fuzzed unlockTime plus the sent value; the bug sets balance to zero always, violating this invariant.

For any account, after a non-zero 'Put' call, the recorded balance in 'Acc' must be at least the msg.value sent; the bug sets balance to zero for every Put, so it breaks this for any positive payment.
After any call to Put with a positive msg.value, the caller's Acc balance must be greater than zero; the buggy version sets it to zero, violating this for any positive payment.
After a call to Put with a positive msg.value, the caller's Acc balance must be at least the msg.value sent; the buggy version sets balance to zero, breaking this invariant.
After any Put call, the caller's Acc balance must be non‐zero whenever msg.value is strictly positive; the mutant assigns zero for every Put, violating the invariant for any positive payment.

In the reference contract, a Collect after a Put that triggers a re-entrant Collect cannot cause the balance to underflow or drop below the pre-Put balance; the buggy version allows re-entrancy that can drain more than the account's balance, causing an underflow that reverts on subtraction or leaves a corrupted (very large) balance state.

In the correct version, after a Put call, the caller's balance cannot exceed the sum of their previous balance and the msg.value sent; the buggy version with disabled nonReentrant_ allows a re-entrant Collect during Put to drain funds and leave the balance lower than the previous balance alone.
After any sequence of external calls, the sum of all account balances recorded in Acc cannot exceed the contract's ETH balance; the buggy version allows re-entrant drains that break this invariant.

After a Put call, the caller's balance must be at least the msg.value sent; the buggy version allows a re-entrant Collect during Put to drain funds and leave the caller's balance below the sent msg.value.

After calling Put with a non-zero msg.value, the contract's ETH balance must strictly increase relative to its balance before the call; the buggy version allows a re-entrant Collect to drain funds during Put, leaving the contract's ETH balance lower than before.
A successful Collect call must always reduce the caller's balance by the requested amount.
